// Room "P3 dining room" (interior designer's part): inner air x58..60, y2..4, z14..17 (plan.md FLOORS, rooms.json).
// Layout: the dining table is the focal piece, on the middle column x59 with a chair at each end (north and south).
// The east column x60 holds a barrel dresser at z14..15 and stays clear at z16..17, and the west column x58 is the
// lane from the cased opening (x57) and round to the kitchen door (59,18), so every cell stays reachable.
// Light: one lantern hangs over the table (the focal piece sits in the brightest light), one over the west lane.
import { layers } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";

export function build(g) {
  // legend: one character per block; '.' is left as it is (free floor)
  const legend = {
    c: ["oak_stairs", { facing: "north", half: "bottom" }], // chair north of the table, back to the north wall
    s: ["oak_stairs", { facing: "south", half: "bottom" }], // chair south of the table, back to the south
    f: "oak_fence", // table leg (the post)
    t: ["oak_slab", { type: "top" }], // table top, sits on the post at y3
    k: "barrel", // dresser on the east wall
    p: "potted_poppy", // on the dresser's top face
    L: ["lantern", { hanging: "true" }], // hangs from the upper floor's block at y5
  };
  layers(g, [58, 2, 14], legend, [
    // y2: floor layer of the furniture (rows z14..17, columns x58..60)
    [".ck", ".fk", ".s.", "..."],
    // y3: table top and the pot on the dresser
    ["..p", ".t.", "...", "..."],
    // y4: lanterns (rows z14..17)
    ["...", ".L.", "L..", "..."],
  ]);
}

input.summary:
parts/room-24.mjs (P3 dining room) is unchanged: its 9 furniture writes are still REFUSED and nothing is placed.
OFF-PALETTE is already clean: all six block ids are in palette.json.
make.sh runs and writes build.nbt (5948 cells), but the dining room contributes nothing to it.
left: REFUSED (9 writes) cannot be cleared inside parts/room-24.mjs. Every cell of the room's footprint (x58..60, z14..17, y1..5) is already owned by shell-west.mjs: house() fills the interior y2..top with air, the ground floor at y1, and the upper floor at y5 over x52..60 z14..20. runParts locks air as well as solid blocks, so moving a write to another cell in the room does not help, and no cell in the room is free. I did not write past the lock, since that would defeat the guard.

The fix belongs upstream in parts/shell-west.mjs (not mine to edit): house() should leave the interior unwritten, not fill it with air, so room parts can furnish their own cells. The same lock also covers the wall openings that shell-west leaves as air (windows, doors, shutters), so the glazing/doors part will be refused too. That part is still a stub, so this is unverified.
The other room parts are stubs (0 placed) and show no refusals yet, but they will hit the same lock once they write anything.
finished is false: the part is not built, although make.sh does produce a whole build.nbt.

waste.what: Traced the 9 refusals by hand: read shell-west.mjs house(), runParts' lock code and the parts report to find which earlier part owned the cells, then checked each room cell against the owned volume.
waste.cost: about 6 tool calls and several minutes of reading; the owner was shell-west's house() air fill, which the report never names
waste.tool: parts-report refusedAt should carry the owning part's name (e.g. 'owned by shell west (plots 0-3)'), and a preflight should flag any room footprint that an earlier part already owns, before the room designers run.

waste.what: Ran `$MCD blocks --check` without a version flag, so it checked against the latest version (26.3), not the server's 1.21.1.
waste.cost: one wasted check; the palette result is still valid because all the ids exist in 1.21.1
waste.tool: make the server version the default for `mcd blocks --check` (here: `--version 1.21.1`, or read it from the build's DataVersion), so the check matches the server.

companions.task: Own the shell walls and interior: decide how the interior and wall openings are left unwritten (not air-filled) in shell-west, so room and fitting parts can place their own blocks without a lock conflict.
Once the openings are left open, set the window panes and the door and shutter fittings in the wall cells that shell-west currently locks as air.
